items.text: Scheduler.pause(tag) and Scheduler.resume(tag) were added on 2026-11-03 on branch `feature/pause-jobs` (uncommitted when reported) so all jobs with a tag can be stopped during maintenance windows without cancelling and re-adding them. They set a public `paused` attribute on `Job`, which `run_pending` checks to skip paused jobs. Module-level `schedule.pause` and `schedule.resume` wrappers were also added and listed in `docs/reference.rst`. Tests in `test_schedule.py` cover paused jobs being skipped while other tags still run, running again after resume, and pause/resume of an unknown tag being harmless. The full suite of 84 tests passed.

items.text: Pause semantics (implemented 2026-11-03): after `resume`, a job whose time passed during the pause runs once on the next `run_pending`, and missed runs are not replayed, consistent with existing `run_pending` behavior. Pausing or resuming an unknown tag is a no-op that doesn't raise. `run_all` still runs paused jobs, because only `run_pending` was asked to skip them; this is noted in the `pause` docstring and left open for the user to decide, and changing it would be a one-line change.

items.text: `Scheduler.get_jobs_for(func)` returns every scheduled job whose function is `func`, regardless of args or schedule, so callers no longer need to hold Job objects just to cancel them later. It is covered by `test_get_jobs_for` in test_schedule.py and documented in docs/reference.rst. It was committed on 2026-11-03 on branch `feature/jobs-by-func` as f08ccd5 (authored by Bench User, co-authored with Claude; not pushed, no PR), with 82 tests passing; bound-method matching is not tested.

items.text: The at() scheduling method gained seconds-level precision in January 2019 (Nathan Wailes): it accepts 1-second precision timestamps and supports recurring tasks like every().minute.at(':30'), fixed the at(':SS') bug, validates format by selected unit, rejects whitespace and non-string input with an exception, and docstrings/READMEs were updated after the two-colon every().minute.at('::SS') syntax was removed. Later bugfixes (Nov 2020 to Jan 2021): hour.at('MM:SS') parsing (#290) and tuesday.at('HH:MM:SS') not running today (#331/#337).

The FAQ was repeatedly expanded between 2014 and 2018 with common usage questions: handling jobs that throw exceptions, running a job only once (fixes #49), jobqueue.task_done() for threaded queues (#134), and a fix referencing #37.

items.text: Job tagging was added in October-November 2016 by Zerrossetto to allow clearing subsets of jobs easily. Follow-ups: type enforcement for tags, using a set instead of a list, handling repeated tags, slice assignment to preserve external references to self.jobs, handling jobs that cancel their own scheduling, and generator expressions. Documented in the FAQ.

Python version support evolved over time: Python 2.7 and 3.5 dropped and 3.9 added (#416, Jan 2021); 3.10 and 3.11 supported and 3.6 dropped (#575, April 2023); 3.12 support added (#606, Dec 2023); dependency on the old mock package removed (#622, April 2024).

Test infrastructure includes a mock_datetime helper that patches datetime to make time-dependent scheduling tests deterministic. It began as a decorator and was switched to context-manager ('with') support in September 2013, and was used to refactor run_pending and other tests.

items.text: Timezone support was a sustained initiative from April 2022 to May 2024: timezone support for .at() (#517), a fix for schedule being off when using .at with timezone (#583), pytz added as a dependency (#601), more timezone tests (#602), improved timezone handling in next_run (#604), and further bugfixes (#623).

Jobs can stop themselves by returning the CancelJob sentinel rather than a falsy value. This was introduced in August–September 2013 (commit 09dab10, then 2c646ff replaced `False` with `CancelJob` and renamed `remove`), followed by unit tests and a cancel_job bug fix. The module-level cancel_job delegates to the Scheduler class's cancel_job (edabdc5).
